newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: BolsWessanen embarrassed by insider case arrest.
newsitem.headline: BolsWessanen embarrassed by insider case arrest.

text.p: Dutch food and drinks group BolsWessanen said on Friday it was "shocked and embarrassed" at Tuesday's arrest of a company executive on suspicion of insider trading, and added it expected no more arrests among company personnel in the case.
A BolsWessanen spokesman declined to name the suspect directly, identifying him by the initials T.J. van N, and saying he was director of business developments.
BolsWessanen's 1995 annual report lists its director of business developments as T.J. (Teun) van Noort.

"We have sent an internal message to our employees saying we are completely embarrased and shocked (at the news of the arrest)," said company secretary Arie Kwak. "We don't expect any other people from BolsWessanen are suspected in the case."

The year-long investigation into the beleagured drinks concern was sparked by exceptionally heavy trading in BolsWessanen put options on July 3, 1995. The next day, the firm announced a steep profit drop.
In recent weeks, three other people have been arrested in connection with the case.

Dutch news agency ANP reported on Friday one of the suspects was a former director of Duif Convenience Foods, which was incorporated into Wessanen in October 1991. Wessanen merged with drinks group Bols in 1993.
The Dutch prosecutor's office declined to comment on the case.
